C OV E R L E T T E R
The RPL Assessor
Department of Communication Design Design Faculty · 2024

I am writing to submit my Recognition of Prior Learning portfolio in support of my application for the Bachelor of Arts in Design (Communication Design). My nine years of professional practice have equipped me with knowledge, skills, and competencies equivalent to those expected of a graduate of this programme.

My design journey spans brand identity, editorial design, typography, photography, illustration, UX/UI, and motion graphics — working for commercial clients, NGOs, government bodies, and cultural institutions. What distinguishes my practice is its research foundation and African-centred methodology.
This portfolio documents evidence across seven structured parts: Designer Profile, Evidence of Learning, Design Portfolio, Professional Practice, Research & Writing, Awards, and Supporting Documents.

A Design Journey Rooted in Research and Practice
"Design is not mere decoration — it is the architecture of lived meaning."
Nine years of professional practice across brand identity, editorial design, typography, photography, UX/UI, and motion graphics — spanning commercial, cultural, governmental, and community sectors.

This portfolio is organised into seven parts documenting the full breadth of skills, knowledge, and professional competencies acquired through formal education, independent learning, and sustained practice.
Each section maps directly to the qualification outcomes for BA Design (Communication Design), supported by project evidence, reflective writing, and professional documentation.

Client-facing professional practice has been the most demanding and rewarding teacher. Working across 20+projects for commercial clients, NGOs,and government departments has developed my capacity for brief analysis, stakeholder communication, iterative design development, and quality production under real-world constraints.

Photography is both a profession and a research method in my practice. Nine years of documentary, portrait, product, and environmental photography have developed a sophisticated visual languageand post-production workflow.
Photography has sharpened my understanding of light, composition, narrative, and visual hierarchy.

Managing farm operations and property portfolios for three years developed critical transferable competencies: financial management, systems thinking, team leadership, logistical planning, and decision-making under uncertainty.
Theseexperiences cultivated professional discipline and the ability to manage complex multi-variable projects.

Service as a Community Advisory Board member developed my capacity for ethical reasoning, stakeholder consultation, and community-centred communication. This experience directly informs my approach to social impact
design —ensuring that visual communication serves the communities it represents.

typography, photography, UX/UI, and motion graphics have produced a body of work demonstrating sustained graduate-level design competency. Projects span commercial, cultural, governmental, and social impact sectors.
Photography is both a professional service and a research methodology in my practice. Documentary, portrait, and environmental imagery inform visual

D E S I G N P H I L O S O P H Y & S T R E N G T H S

My design practice is driven by curiosity, research,and a commitment to solving meaningful communication problems. Rather than beginning with aesthetics, I begin with understanding —investigating the social, cultural, historical, and behavioural context surrounding a design challenge.
Transforming abstract ideas into clear visual communication systems —research informs every design decision.
Immersing in historical, cultural, social, and visual references before generating ideas, ensuring work is informed and meaningful.
Noticing subtle patterns, relationships, and opportunities —identifying communication problems and discovering unexpected inspiration.
Sustaining deep concentration for extended periods, enabling thorough iteration and technically resolved final outcomes.
Solving complex communication challenges through clear design thinking. Effective design reduces complexity —solutions are elegant and efficient.
Creating compelling outcomes with limited resources —transforming simple materials or constraints into meaningful design solutions.

Gauta Eteng SAG12
Behaviour ChangeCampaign — Art Direction
The Gauta Eteng SAG12campaign represents one of the strongest examples of my capabilities as a conceptual designer and art director. The project
demonstrates my ability to synthesise research, systems thinking, visual storytelling, branding, editorial design, and public communication into a cohesive campaign.

Rather than approaching the brief solely as a graphic design exercise, I developed a comprehensive communication strategy rooted in South African social and environmental contexts —applying behaviour change theory to create a campaign that resonatesauthentically with its target communities.

S E C T I O N 1 6

Researchis the foundation of my design practice. Before generating any visual responseto a brief, I invest significant time in understanding the problem domain —its history, audience, cultural context, and visual landscape.
Academic and professional texts informing theoretical context for each project.
Systematic analysis of the visual landscape within each project's market or sector.
Benchmarking against comparable visual identities, publications, or interfaces.
Curated visual references establishing tone, palette, typography, and aesthetic direction.
Interviews, surveys, and observation to understand audience needs and behaviours.
User models and experience maps informing communication strategy and design decisions.
Documented design processfrom brief through to final outcome, with reflective annotations.
Structured problem-solving framework applied consistently acrossall project phases.

My researchapproach is informed by Design Thinking methodology, African-centred inquiry practices, and the principle that effective communication design is always grounded in deep understanding of context, community, and purpose.
